readings.title: The Cave of Adullam
readings.subtitle: The Gathering of the Discontented and Mighty
readings.text: [1 Samuel 22:1] And Dawid departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. And his brothers and all his father’s house heard it, and they went down to him there. [2] And everyone who was in distress, and everyone who was in debt, and everyone who was discontented, gathered to him. And he became captain over them. And there were about four hundred men with him. [1 Chronicles 12:8] And some of the Gadites separated themselves to Dawid at the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty brave men, men trained for battle, who could handle shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions, and were as swift as gazelles on the mountains: [9] Ezer the first, Obadyah the second, Eliab the third, [10] Mishmannah the fourth, Yirmeyah the fifth, [11] Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh, [12] Yohanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth, [13] Yirmeyah the tenth, Makbannai the eleventh. [14] These were from the sons of Gad, captains of the army. The least was over a hundred, and the greatest was over a thousand. [15] These are the ones who passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yarden in the first month, when it had overflowed all its banks, and they put to flight <dn>את</dn> all those in the valleys, to the east and to the west. [16] And some of the children of Binyamin and Yehudah came to the stronghold to Dawid. [17] And Dawid went out to meet them, and answered and said to them, “If you have come peaceably to me to help me, my heart is united with you. But if to betray me to my enemies, since there is no wrong in my hands, let the <dn>Elohim</dn> of our fathers look and reprove.” [18] And the <dn>Spirit</dn> came upon <dn>את</dn> Amasai, chief of the captains, and he said, “We are yours, O Dawid, and with you, O son of Yishai! Peace, peace to you, and peace to your helpers! For your <dn>Elohim</dn> helps you.” So Dawid received them, and made them captains of the troop.

readings.title: Prayers from the Cave
readings.subtitle: David's Cry for Deliverance and Favour
readings.text: [Psalm 57:1] Show favour to me, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, show favour to me! For in <dn>You</dn> my being has taken refuge; And in the shadow of <dn>Your</dn> wings I take refuge, Until destruction passes by. [2] I cry out to the <dn>Most High Elohim</dn>, To <dn>El</dn> who is perfecting all matters for me. [3] <dn>He</dn> sends from the heavens and saves me; <dn>He</dn> reproaches the one who would swallow me up. Selah. <dn>Elohim</dn> sends forth <dn>His</dn> loving-commitment and <dn>His</dn> truth. [4] My being is among lions; I lie among those who are set on fire, Sons of men whose teeth are spears and arrows, And their tongue a sharp sword. [5] Be exalted, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, above the heavens; Let <dn>Your</dn> esteem be above all the earth. [6] They have prepared a net for my steps; My being was bowed down; They have dug a pit before me; They have fallen into the midst of it! Selah. [7] My heart is steadfast, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, my heart is steadfast; I sing and I praise. [8] Awake, my esteem! Awake, lute and lyre! I awake the dawn. [9] I give thanks to <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>Master</dn>, among the peoples; I sing to <dn>You</dn> among the nations. [10] For <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment is great unto the heavens, And <dn>Your</dn> truth unto the clouds. [11] Be exalted, O <dn>Elohim</dn>, above the heavens; Let <dn>Your</dn> esteem be above all the earth. [Psalm 142:1] I cry to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with my voice; With my voice I pray to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for favour. [2] I pour out my complaint before <dn>Him</dn>; I declare my distress before <dn>Him</dn>. [3] When my spirit grew faint within me, Then <dn>You</dn> knew my path. In the way in which I walk They have hidden a snare for me. [4] Look to the right and see, For there is no one who recognises me; Refuge has failed me; No one cares for my being. [5] I cried out to <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>; I said, “<dn>You</dn> are my refuge, My portion in the land of the living. [6] “Listen to my cry, For I am brought very low; Deliver me from my persecutors, For they are stronger than I. [7] “Bring my being out of prison, To give thanks to <dn>Your Name</dn>. Let the righteous gather around me, Because <dn>You</dn> deal bountifully with me.”

readings.title: The Forest of Hereth
readings.subtitle: A Prophet's Direction and a King's Paranoia
readings.text: [1 Samuel 22:3] And Dawid went from there to Mitspah of Moab, and he said to the sovereign of Moab, “Please let my father and mother come here with you, till I know what <dn>Elohim</dn> does for me.” [4] So he brought them <dn>את</dn> before the sovereign of Moab, and they dwelt with him all the time that Dawid was in the stronghold. [5] And the prophet Gad said to Dawid, “Do not stay in the stronghold, depart, and go to the land of Yehudah.” So Dawid departed and went into the forest of Hereth. [6] And Sha'ul heard that Dawid and the men who were <dn>את</dn> with him had been discovered. And Sha'ul was sitting in Gibeah under a tamarisk tree in Ramah, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing about him. [7] And Sha'ul said to his servants who stood about him, “Listen now, you Benjaminites! Does the son of Yishai give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make <dn>את</dn> all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds? [8] “For all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who reveals to me that my son has made a covenant with the son of Yishai. And there is not one of you who is sorry for me or reveals to me that my son has stirred up <dn>את</dn> my servant against me, to lie in wait, as it is this day.” [9] And Doeg the Edomite, who was set over the servants of Sha'ul, answered and said, “I saw <dn>את</dn> the son of Yishai going to Nob, to Ahimelek son of Ahitub. [10] “And he inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for him, and gave him provisions, and gave him <dn>את</dn> the sword of Golyath the Philistine.”

readings.title: A Maskil Concerning Doeg
readings.subtitle: Trusting in El Amidst Treachery
readings.text: [Psalm 52:1] Why do you boast in evil, O mighty man? The loving-commitment of <dn>El</dn> is all day long. [2] Your tongue plots destruction, Like a sharp razor, working deceit. [3] You have loved evil more than good, Falsehood more than speaking righteousness. Selah. [4] You have loved all devouring words, O deceitful tongue. [5] Also, <dn>El</dn> breaks you down forever; <dn>He</dn> takes you and plucks you out of the tent, And <dn>He</dn> uproots you from the land of the living. Selah. [6] And the righteous see and fear, And laugh at him, saying, [7] “See the man who did not make <dn>Elohim</dn> his strength, But trusted in the abundance of his riches, He was strong in his destruction.” [8] But I am like a green olive tree in the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>; I have trusted in the loving-commitment of <dn>Elohim</dn> forever and ever. [9] I thank <dn>You</dn> forever, Because <dn>You</dn> have done it; And in the presence of <dn>Your</dn> lovingly-committed ones I wait on <dn>Your Name</dn>, for it is good.

readings.title: The Massacre at Nob
readings.subtitle: Saul's Vengeance Against the Priests of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [1 Samuel 22:11] And the sovereign sent someone to call <dn>את</dn> Ahimelek the priest, son of Ahitub, and <dn>את</dn> all his father’s house, the priests who were in Nob. And they all came to the sovereign. [12] And Sha'ul said, “Hear now, son of Ahitub!” And he answered, “Here I am, my master.” [13] And Sha'ul said to him, “Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Yishai, in that you have given him bread and a sword, and have inquired of <dn>Elohim</dn> for him, to rise against me, to lie in wait, as it is this day?” [14] And Ahimelek answered the sovereign and said, “And who among all your servants is as trustworthy as Dawid, who is the sovereign’s son-in-law, and is admitted to your council, and is esteemed in your house? [15] “Did I begin to inquire of <dn>Elohim</dn> for him today? Far be it from me! Let not the sovereign impute a matter to his servant, nor to any in the house of my father. For your servant knew naught of all this, little or much.” [16] And the sovereign said, “You shall certainly die, Ahimelek, you and all your father’s house.” [17] And the sovereign said to the guards who stood about him, “Turn and kill the priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, because their hand also is with Dawid, and because they knew when he fled and did not reveal it to me.” But the servants of the sovereign would not put out <dn>את</dn> their hands to fall upon the priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [18] And the sovereign said to Doeg, “You turn and fall upon the priests!” And Doeg the Edomite turned and fell upon the priests, and struck down on that day eighty-five men wearing a linen shoulder garment. [19] And he struck <dn>את</dn> Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword, both man and woman, child and nursing infant, ox and donkey and sheep, with the edge of the sword. [20] But one of the sons of Ahimelek son of Ahitub, named Ebyathar, escaped and fled after Dawid. [21] And Ebyathar reported to Dawid that Sha'ul had killed <dn>את</dn> the priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [22] And Dawid said to Ebyathar, “I knew that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would certainly inform Sha'ul. I am responsible for all the lives of your father’s house. [23] “Stay with me, do not fear. For he who seeks <dn>את</dn> my life seeks <dn>את</dn> your life, but with me you are safe.”

readings.title: The Deliverance of Qe'ilah
readings.subtitle: David Inquires of YeHoVaH and Saves the City
readings.text: [1 Samuel 23:1] And they reported to Dawid, saying, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Qe'ilah, and they are robbing <dn>את</dn> the threshing-floors.” [2] And Dawid inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Shall I go and smite these Philistines?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Dawid, <dq>“Go and smite the Philistines, and save <dn>את</dn> Qe'ilah.”</dq> [3] But Dawid’s men said to him, “Look, we are afraid here in Yehudah. How much more then if we go to Qe'ilah against the armies of the Philistines?” [4] And Dawid inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> yet again. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered him and said, <dq>“Rise up, go down to Qe'ilah, for <dn>I</dn> am giving <dn>את</dn> the Philistines into your hand.”</dq> [5] And Dawid and his men went to Qe'ilah and fought against the Philistines, and led away <dn>את</dn> their livestock and struck them with a great blow. Thus Dawid saved <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Qe'ilah. [6] And it came to be, when Ebyathar son of Ahimelek fled to Dawid at Qe'ilah, he went down with an ephod in his hand. [7] And it was reported to Sha'ul that Dawid had come to Qe'ilah. And Sha'ul said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has delivered <dn>את</dn> him into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a town that has gates and bars.” [8] And Sha'ul summoned <dn>את</dn> all the people to battle, to go down to Qe'ilah, to besiege Dawid and his men. [9] And Dawid knew that Sha'ul was plotting evil against him. And he said to Ebyathar the priest, “Bring the ephod here.” [10] And Dawid said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra'el, <dn>Your</dn> servant has heard for certain that Sha'ul is seeking to come to Qe'ilah to destroy the city for my sake. [11] “Would the masters of Qe'ilah surrender me into his hand? Would Sha'ul come down, as <dn>Your</dn> servant has heard? O <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra'el, I pray, let <dn>Your</dn> servant know.” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“He is coming down.”</dq> [12] And Dawid said, “Would the masters of Qe'ilah surrender <dn>את</dn> me and <dn>את</dn> my men into the hand of Sha'ul?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“They would surrender you.”</dq>
